frontier.hypothesis: Cluster E (7 diffs) closes if the tail pointer's birth is delayed 2 more insns beyond what B_ptr_late already buys - span(qty0) 26 -> <= 24 - without adding an instruction.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c qty_compare_1 priority floor_log2(refs)*refs*size/(death-birth)*10000 with ties by ascending qty number; birth is the quantity's first reference in the post-sched1 stream, so anything sched1 can legally emit ahead of the ashift/addu pushes it later. The measured window is span <= 24 and B_ptr_late reached 26.
frontier.next_probe: Start from B_ptr_late (tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s7/probe.py B_ptr_late) and enumerate what else can honestly precede the pointer in block 41: the two `& 0xFFF` index computations and the `+ 0x400` bias are the only independent work available. Measure each reorder with sandbox AND with tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s7/qty41.py (BB2_QTY_DEBUG block-41 dump) - the dump is the ground truth, since a birth vector is necessary but not sufficient. If no reorder reaches birth >= 8, re-run inverse.py local at depth 3 to see whether a 2-atom vector (birth + refs) opens a cheaper door.

frontier.hypothesis: Cluster A (12 diffs) closes if temp_s3's live length rises from 14 to exactly 20 or 21, or if arg1's falls from 92 into [38,65]; the joint map means a partial move in each can be combined instead of finding one big lever.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocno_compare on pri = floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs*size/reg_live_length*10000 with ties by lower allocno number. Live length is a property of the post-sched1 INSN ORDER, not of the insn COUNT, so both dials are reachable by reordering alone - the 215==215 budget does not foreclose them.
frontier.next_probe: Build the global analogue of this session's local dial: take the joint table (L143 10..21 x L73 38..98) as the acceptance test, and for each candidate source reordering measure L73/L143 straight out of the model (extract.py then read flow.livelen_flow) rather than out of the score. frontier.hypothesis: The single PRE-RA instruction (ours beqz, target bnez) is the same jump2/cross-jump question as clusters B and D, and one instrumented .jump2 read can settle all three.
frontier.mechanism: jump.c find_cross_jump decides which of two identical tails survives and which is redirected; when the surviving copy is the late one the rejection chain's last branch inverts sense, which is exactly a beqz/bnez swap and one relocated block. reorg.c fill_simple_delay_slots then can only leave `li v0,1` in the `j`'s delay slot when the surviving block carries a label with real predecessors.
frontier.next_probe: Dump .jump2 for the current candidate (pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_800283D0 - the dumps land in tmp/grind/func_800283D0/dumps/) and read which block find_cross_jump KEEPS and which it redirects at the beqz site; then look for a source arrangement in which the chain-fallthrough copy is the survivor.
